issues.legal_issue: A person who purchases land after publication of an acquisition notification is not entitled under the government policy to an alternative site as the owner whose land was acquired.
material_facts: The claim was made in a writ petition for an alternative site under government policy on the basis that land had been acquired for a public purpose.
The claimant was not the owner when the acquisition notification was published, but became the owner before the acquisition was finalized.
The government policy treated the owner on the date of notification as the person entitled to an alternative site.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to an alternative site; the direction granting one was quashed and the writ petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the government policy, the person whose land was acquired means the owner on the date the notification under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was published. A subsequent purchaser may claim compensation through the rights acquired from the predecessor, but does not qualify as the owner for allotment of an alternative site. The Court also referred to its prior view while considering a Full Bench judgment of the Delhi High Court, without identifying that case in this judgment.

predicates.alternative_site_writ_claim: A claimant sought an alternative site by filing a writ petition under a government policy for acquired land.
predicates.land_acquired_for_public_purpose: The land in question was acquired for a public purpose.

predicates.later_purchaser_not_eligible_for_alterna: A person who purchased the land after the acquisition notification is not eligible for an alternative site under the policy.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks an alternative site for land acquired for a public purpose and bought it after the acquisition notice, the claimant is not eligible for an alternative site.
